🇲🇽🌎 SHEINBAUM TO OPEN A NATIONAL DEBATE ON REGULATING BIG TECH AND AI

After the World Cup, Sheinbaum will launch a national discussion on regulating social media and artificial intelligence — not censorship, but confronting who owns the platforms and who controls the algorithms. "Who controls artificial intelligence? What beneficial uses does it have? What should concern us?" she asked, opening the table to specialists, legislators, media and parents. Digital sovereignty is now on the agenda.

🔥🇲🇽 MEXICO'S AUDITOR FILES 21 CRIMINAL CASES OVER 600M PESOS IN STOLEN PUBLIC MONEY

Mexico's Superior Audit Office (ASF) filed 21 criminal complaints with the FGR over more than 600 million pesos in damage to the treasury, hitting around 30 officials across all three levels of government in the first review of Sheinbaum's opening year. It's the first fruit of an April 21 oversight reform that lets the ASF investigate and denounce without waiting for the full audit cycle to close.

🇲🇽⚽ "Pick up your trash — it's the cleaning workers who have to collect it all." "Pick up your trash when you leave, because it's the cleaning workers who afterward have to do all this collecting." — President Claudia Sheinbaum Ahead of Mexico vs. Ecuador, the president wished the national team strength — "mucha fuerza" — and asked fans to celebrate with respect and clean up after themselves.

🇲🇽✊ 2,275 new hospital beds and renovated operating rooms across the public system. "2,275 electric beds in 33 hospital units, and three renovated operating rooms in Monterrey." — Martí Batres, ISSSTE Director The bed rollout cost 205 million pesos; the new Monterrey operating rooms, fitted with 85 new machines, cost 93 million. Rebuilding a public health system left to decay through the neoliberal decades.

🇲🇽✊ Mexico nearly doubled its public MRI capacity in a year. "We went from 80 to 150 studies a week." — Zoé Robledo, IMSS Director The IMSS installed 17 new MRI machines — 11 at 1.5 teslas, 6 at 3 teslas. The newer units also cut helium use from 100 liters to just 7 per machine. More diagnoses, shorter waits, lower cost — in the public system.

🇲🇽✊ Mexico's first public fetal surgery unit is operating on babies before birth — for free. "The country's first public Fetal Surgery Unit is already operating in Villahermosa: three fetuses with gastroschisis operated on successfully." — Alejandro Svarch, IMSS Bienestar The unit is part of a 4-billion-peso investment in 174 high-specialty machines. Surgery this complex used to exist only in private hospitals. Now it's public, and families pay nothing.

🇲🇽✊ Undetectable = untransmittable. And in Mexico, the treatment is free. "A person who is undetectable no longer transmits the disease. Treatment is free for everyone." — David Kershenobich, Health Secretary Around 430,000 people live with HIV in Mexico; about 70% — some 302,000 — are diagnosed and receive uninterrupted treatment at no cost. The goal now: reach the 128,000 who don't yet know. Public health as a right, not a market.

🇲🇽🇻🇪 Mexico is flying emergency power plants to earthquake-hit Venezuela today. "Today the emergency power plants and other equipment and supplies are being sent — by plane." — President Claudia Sheinbaum After 7.2 and 7.5 quakes killed more than 1,700 people and injured some 5,000, Mexico is sending seven power plants by air and preparing a Navy ship with food and supplies. Mexican Defense crews coordinated on the ground with Venezuelan authorities. Solidarity, no conditions attached.
